_comment: What this app relies on Microsoft Graph to keep providing.
Every type and property here is one this app writes into a request
body or reads out of a response. GraphContract.Tests.ps1 checks each
of them against Graph's own published $metadata, so the day Microsoft
renames or removes one, a scheduled CI run says so - instead of a
deployment failing in somebody's tenant with a 400 nobody can place.
What it catches: a property or type that is REMOVED or RENAMED.
What it does not catch, and this was measured rather than assumed:
a property Graph still declares but no longer accepts.
minimumSupportedOperatingSystem is exactly that - replaced in practice
by minimumSupportedWindowsRelease, rejected by the API, and still
sitting in beta $metadata today. So is applicableArchitectures, which
the tenant refuses inside a PATCH; see the notes in
not what works, and only a live call against a real tenant can tell
Adding a property here is a claim that the app would break without it.
Anything the app merely passes through untouched does not belong.
